items.title: Ramadan
items.importance: Ramadan is the month in which the Quran was revealed—a guided mercy and clear criterion for humanity.
items.virtues: The gates of Paradise are opened, devils are chained, and every good deed is multiplied.
items.recommendedActs: Fast sincerely, increase Quran recitation, give charity, pray Taraweeh, and seek Laylatul Qadr in the last ten nights.

items.title: Eid al-Fitr
items.importance: Eid al-Fitr marks the completion of Ramadan and gratitude to Allah for enabling the fast.
items.virtues: It is a day of joy, community, and thankfulness after a month of worship and self-discipline.
items.recommendedActs: Pay Zakat al-Fitr, perform Eid prayer, wear your best clothes, greet others, and visit family while maintaining Islamic manners.

items.title: Eid al-Adha
items.importance: Eid al-Adha commemorates the devotion of Ibrahim (AS) and the rites of Hajj during Dhul Hijjah.
items.virtues: It teaches sacrifice, obedience to Allah, and care for those in need through the udhiyah (sacrifice).
items.recommendedActs: Perform Eid prayer, offer sacrifice if able, share meat with the poor, and increase takbir in the first ten days of Dhul Hijjah.

items.title: Hajj season
items.importance: Hajj is a once-in-a-lifetime pillar for those who are able—a profound journey of unity and submission.
items.virtues: A accepted Hajj brings forgiveness of sins and renewal of purpose. The plain of Arafah is the heart of Hajj.
items.recommendedActs: Those not performing Hajj can fast on the Day of Arafah, increase dhikr, and make du'a for those at the sacred sites.

items.title: Ashura
items.importance: The 10th of Muharram is the day Allah saved Musa (AS) and his people from Pharaoh.
items.virtues: Fasting on Ashura expiates the sins of the previous year (when combined with fasting a day before or after, per the Sunnah).
items.recommendedActs: Fast the 9th and 10th of Muharram if possible, reflect on Allah's help to the oppressed, and increase gratitude.

items.title: Laylatul Qadr
items.importance: Laylatul Qadr is better than a thousand months—it is the night the Quran's revelation began.
items.virtues: Worship on this single night can surpass decades of reward. The angels descend with peace until Fajr.
items.recommendedActs: Seek it in the odd nights of the last ten days of Ramadan through prayer, Quran, du'a, and istighfar.

items.title: Jumu'ah (Friday)
items.importance: Friday is the best day on which the sun rises. It includes a weekly congregational prayer and a weekly reminder.
items.virtues: There is a moment on Friday when du'a is accepted. Sins between Fridays are forgiven for those who bathe and attend with sincerity.
items.recommendedActs: Perform ghusl, wear clean clothes, arrive early to the masjid, listen attentively to the khutbah, and increase salawat upon the Prophet ﷺ.
